en: O Śrīpāda, O Śrīvallabha, you who are eternally endowed with splendor, O God of gods, protect us whom you have granted.
O Sukīrti, who removes the afflictions grasped at as real entities, lift us up from this terrible suffering; homage to you!
You are our mother, you are our father, you are our refuge; you are our protector, the provider of security and well-being, and you are our supreme teacher.
O Lord, you who are the universal form, you are our everything; deliver us from this terrible misery—salutations to you!
O Swift One, you take away evil, torment, physical disease, mental affliction, wretchedness, fear, and distress.
O Lord, look upon us as our protector; deliver us from this terrible and painful calamity; salutations to You!

There is no other protector, no giver, and no sustainer; O God, you alone are the refuge and the remover of suffering. O Puruṣottama, show favor to the descendants of Atri; deliver us from this terrible distress—salutations to you!

O embodiment of all bliss, grant us love for the Dharma, right understanding, devotion to the Divine, association with the virtuous, worldly enjoyment, liberation, and detachment from worldly existence; deliver us from this terrible suffering—salutations to You!
Whoever, being self-restrained, recites with devotion these five verses that increase the auspiciousness of the world, shall become dear to Śrī Datta.
Thus ends the "Hymn for Deliverance from the Torment of Aghora," composed by the venerable Vāsudevānandasarasvatī.
